BREAKING: Global central bank gold purchases rose +62 tonnes YoY in Q2 2026, to 289 tonnes, the biggest quarterly addition since Q4 2024.

Quarter-over-quarter, gold purchases surged +231 tonnes, or +407%.

Year-to-date, central banks have acquired +345 tonnes of gold.

Poland has led these purchases at +82 tonnes, bringing its total reserves to a record 632 tonnes.

Uzbekistan and China followed, adding +41 tonnes and +40 tonnes, respectively, so far this year.

Central banks continue to accumulate gold at a rapid pace.

The most indebted consumer in the developed world is watching home prices fall.

Australian house prices dropped 0.7% in July, the steepest run of declines since 2022, with Sydney down 1.4%. Yet mortgage debt is still growing: total home loans up 7.5% from a year ago, and investor borrowing up 10.4%, the fastest in over a decade.

Prices down while leverage climbs is how negative equity gets built. Three RBA rate hikes this year are finally biting the household balance sheet. When the most leveraged consumer in the developed world cracks, the wealth effect goes into reverse and spending follows it down.

$EWA
